research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and National Data Library sources only; PFA/CSP geography, rate calculation, revisions, classification breaks and rural-urban context; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSP-quarter-offence-code breakdown
verified_claims: the dataset is broken down by CSP
it also includes quarterly period and individual offence-code dimensions
limitations: each dimension must be retained for unique keys
offence codes require the edition-matched reference table

sources.name: Required contextual user guide
verified_claims: the catalogue recommends consulting the crime-statistics user guide with the tables
the guide supplies classification and interpretation context
limitations: catalogue rows alone are insufficient for analysis
user-guide caveats must accompany derived metrics

sources.name: CSP and local-authority coterminosity
verified_claims: in nearly all cases CSP boundaries are coterminous with local-authority areas
CSPs are a principal geography for local recorded-crime publication
limitations: nearly all cases leaves exceptions
boundary reference data must be checked

sources.name: Headline offences by CSP
verified_claims: recorded-crime figures for headline offences are published for each CSP
the output supports local-area comparison
limitations: headline offences are not the complete offence-code inventory
local comparison remains sensitive to recording practice

sources.name: CSP count as of December 2022
verified_claims: the user guide states that there were 314 CSPs in England and Wales as of December 2022
the count is time-specific
limitations: the count must not be assumed current after boundary changes
CSP count is not a parcel count

sources.name: CSP statutory origin
verified_claims: CSPs were established under the Crime and Disorder Act 1998
the statutory context explains their partnership role
limitations: statutory origin does not define current boundaries
legal context is not a crime measure

sources.name: CSP multi-agency membership
verified_claims: CSPs include police health probation and other local agencies
the partnerships develop local crime-reduction strategies
limitations: membership does not imply shared data granularity
strategy participation is not an outcome score

sources.name: Former CDRP terminology
verified_claims: in England CSPs were previously termed Crime and Disorder Reduction Partnerships
historical publications may use the CDRP label
limitations: CDRP and CSP names require date-aware mapping
the terminology change must not create duplicate geographies

sources.name: Region statistical naming from 2011
verified_claims: from 1 April 2011 Government Office Region areas are referred to as regions for statistical purposes
the classification supports regional presentation
limitations: the naming change is not a boundary guarantee
region must not replace PFA or CSP identifiers

sources.name: Rural-urban classifications for CSP and PFA
verified_claims: the user guide applies a three-way rural-urban classification at CSP and PFA levels
the categories support contextual analysis
limitations: classification is contextual rather than a safety outcome
edition and methodology must be stored

sources.name: Rural-80 threshold
verified_claims: Rural-80 districts have at least 80 percent of their population in rural settlements and larger market towns
they are included in the predominantly rural category
limitations: threshold classification is not a continuous rurality score
population and settlement definitions are methodology-specific

sources.name: Rural-50 threshold
verified_claims: Rural-50 districts have at least 50 percent but less than 80 percent of population in rural settlements and larger market towns
they are included in the predominantly rural category
limitations: boundary values must follow the published rule
the category is not a crime-risk estimate

sources.name: Significant-rural threshold
verified_claims: Significant rural districts have more than 37,000 people or more than 26 percent of population in rural settlements and larger market towns
the category sits between predominantly rural and predominantly urban
limitations: the rule contains alternative conditions
the classification must not be inferred from land area alone

sources.name: Major-urban threshold
verified_claims: Major urban districts have either 100,000 people or 50 percent of population in urban areas above 750,000
the category belongs to predominantly urban
limitations: the two-part rule must be preserved
urban classification is not a crime-volume denominator

sources.name: Large-urban threshold
verified_claims: Large urban districts have either 50,000 people or 50 percent of population in urban areas between 250,000 and 750,000
the category belongs to predominantly urban
limitations: the specified population band must be retained
category labels are not interchangeable across methodologies

sources.name: Other-urban threshold
verified_claims: Other urban districts have fewer than 37,000 people or fewer than 26 percent of population in rural settlements and larger market towns
the category belongs to predominantly urban
limitations: the published OR logic must be retained
the classification should not be derived from crime data

sources.name: PFA rural-urban methodology
verified_claims: a different methodology with similar criteria is used for the three-way PFA classification
PFA and CSP classifications are related but not identical
limitations: CSP labels must not be copied to PFA without the official mapping
method version is required

sources.name: No recognised international crime-recording standard
verified_claims: ONS states there are currently no recognised international standards for crime recording
national recording systems are shaped by different legal frameworks
limitations: absence of a standard does not imply unusable national data
international league tables require strong caveats

sources.name: International legal and recording differences
verified_claims: international recorded-crime comparisons are limited by different legal systems
collection and police-recording practices also differ
limitations: raw national rates must not be directly ranked
definitions and recording rules require reconciliation

sources.name: International victimisation-survey differences
verified_claims: national victimisation surveys differ in sampling
reference periods and questions also vary
valid international comparison is therefore difficult
limitations: similar survey aims do not guarantee comparable estimates
methodological harmonisation is required
